extraction.name: POPE
extraction.description: POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation) is an evaluation dataset and method for assessing object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) by prompting them with simple Yes-or-No questions about probing objects.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li (Renmin University of China); Yifan Du (Renmin University of China); Kun Zhou (Renmin University of China); Jinpeng Wang (Meituan Group); Wayne Xin Zhao (Renmin University of China); Ji-Rong Wen (Renmin University of China)
extraction.citeAs: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen. Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models. arXiv:2305.10355v3, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The evaluation dataset was assembled by randomly sampling images from the validation sets of existing datasets (MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA) and constructing polling questions based on ground-truth objects obtained from human annotations or automatic segmentation tools, alongside nonexistent objects sampled via random, popular, or adversarial strategies.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images and annotations from the validation sets of the MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Images from MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA were annotated using the SEEM automatic segmentation tool to extract objects, which were then used to construct Yes/No polling questions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The visual instruction datasets share an unbalanced object distribution where top frequent objects occupy a major part of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The evaluation task cannot measure the overall performance of LVLMs; evaluated on only a part of the validation set which might be affected by data distribution; the matching-based method may fail if LVLMs do not explicitly output Yes/No; automatic segmentation tool labels may be inconsistent with human annotations; only a small number of LVLMs were compared.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Object hallucination hinders the safe use of LVLMs in real-world deployment and may result in unexpected consequences, such as autonomous driving systems making wrong decisions leading to serious safety issues.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Stable, fair and flexible object hallucination evaluation of LVLMs.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: For datasets without annotations, the SEEM automatic segmentation tool was used to infer missing object labels and annotate images to build the evaluation dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The ratio between ground-truth and nonexistent objects was set as 1:1 for label balance. Nonexistent objects were sampled using three strategies: Random Sampling, Popular Sampling (selecting the top-k most frequent objects in the dataset), and Adversarial Sampling (ranking objects by co-occurring frequencies with ground-truth objects and selecting the top-k frequent ones).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The evaluation dataset was filtered to only consider the 80 objects appearing in the MSCOCO segmentation challenge, and the authors randomly selected 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects in the annotations.
